notes.title: Update 0.57 — “The Game Comes Alive!”
notes.content: [p]What’s new[/p][p] Turn Transition – Blink & File Slide[/p][p]Each new turn now begins with a quick blink-to-black, followed by your dossier sliding off-screen and snapping back into place—adding a crisp “page-turn” feel to the flow of play.[/p][p]Hand Entrance / Exit[/p][p]The hand no longer pops in and out of existence. It now glides on-stage from beyond the frame when you hover over cards, and drifts away just as smoothly when you move on.[/p][p]Global Hover Animations[/p][p]Every interactive object—files, books, regions, letters, ballots—now leans toward the camera on hover, giving instant, tactile feedback that begs to be clicked.[/p][p]Multiplayer status[/p][p]We’ve run multiple rounds of network tests: in-game sync is solid, but the lobby UI can still be stubborn. If the “Start Game” or “Ready” buttons stay hidden, let all players sit tight—a two-minute patience test usually sorts itself out.  [/p][p][/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="iFMtrfcn-8U;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]Up next...[/p][p]Our immediate focus:[/p][p]Layering in sound effects for each new animation.[/p][p]Building more events and decisions to keep every turn fresh.[/p][p]Stay tuned—and thanks for helping us shape the demo into something special!![/p]

notes.title: Early Demo Sneak-Peek: 15-Turn Build Now Playable
notes.content:
[p]The very first demo build is live on Steam. It ends at Turn 15 (full game is 24 turns) and still has missing features and known issues, but core systems like the Turn 10 election and revolution mechanics are already playable.[/p][p]Multiplayer is [b]not[/b] reliable yet—random errors may block matches entirely. Single-player should run start-to-finish, but expect rough edges.[/p][p]Please post any bugs, balance notes, or suggestions here on Steam or in our Discord. The more feedback we get now, the cleaner the “official” demo launch will be when we push the full 24-turn build in the next 1-2 weeks.[/p][p]Thanks for helping shape [i]Statecraft: Corrupted Democracy!

notes.title: Context-Aware Tutorial Notes – Learn as You Play
notes.content:
[p][b]Event Description[/b]
Today’s patch adds a step-through tutorial that surfaces short notes exactly when you need them. As soon as the match begins, keyed moments trigger a translucent pop-up; tapping [b]Next[/b] reveals the following hint and, when relevant, temporarily opens the UI panel being explained so you can see each mechanic in action. If you’d rather rehearse before diving in, the same note sequence is available from the Main Menu, and you can reopen it mid-game via the Almanac book on the right. Because the guide progresses at your own pace and never pulls you from the session, it’s perfect for newcomers and veterans who just need a rules refresh. Alongside the tutorial we cleaned up interface text, corrected a few localization slips, and trimmed loading screens so you spend more time governing and less time waiting.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="9Hf6ytiwuyY;full"][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Demo Status Update – Launching End of June
notes.content: [p]Our [i]Statecraft: Corrupted Democracy[/i] demo cleared Valve’s review after Next Fest had already begun. Rather than launch it amid the festival’s demo rush, we’ll make it public in the last week of June. Thanks for waiting, add the game to your wishlist for a heads-up when the demo drops, and feel free to ask questions on the discussion board.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44900026/23760209d5079d9b867d04b319d048879165501c.png"][/img][/p]

notes.content:
Patch Notes
Multiplayer Lobbies

Host your own lobby and invite friends in seconds.

Jump straight into an existing lobby with a single click.

notes.title: Main Menu & Lobby Update!
notes.content:
This patch adds the core quality-of-life features you’ve been waiting for:

🔧 Universal Settings
• Switch language, resolution, and audio levels straight from the brand-new Main Menu.

🎮 Multiplayer Lobby
• Host a fresh online match or reopen an existing one with a single click.

🗂️ Single-Player Flow
• “New Game” and “Load Game” buttons now hook into a streamlined save system for stress-free campaigns.

💬 Context Tooltips
• Hover any icon—instantly see what it does. No more guesswork.

Jump in, tweak your setup, and let us know how the new UI feels!







[previewyoutube=eVom-lmbZMY;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: UI Overhaul: Fresh Fonts, Interactive Cards & A Brand-New Newspaper!
notes.content:
What’s New?
Crisp New Typeface
Every menu, tooltip and headline now sports a cleaner font for better readability.

Paper-Style Action Cards
– Region and event actions are displayed as vintage paper slips.
– Hovering reveals a hand icon that “picks up” the card with a subtle animation, making choices feel tactile.

Iconic Population Breakdown
Culture, ideology and religion shares are now visualized with distinctive icons—instantly see who holds sway in each region and across the nation.

Newspaper Redux
Our in-game gazette has been completely rebuilt: crisper layout, clearer headlines, smoother page turns. Catch a full preview in the video below!

Why It Matters
These changes aim to make every decision more physical, data more digestible and your daily briefing more dramatic. Jump in, test the cards, skim the revamped paper and tell us what you think on Discord!

(More UI polish and quality-of-life tweaks are on the way—stay tuned!)





[previewyoutube=SV2O826afQk;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: 40 New Conditional Events Added!
notes.content:
Description:
In this update, we’ve introduced 40 brand-new events that activate only once when your country stats meet specific conditions (e.g., Economy ≥ 50, Unrest ≤ 50), keeping the experience fresh:

Stat-Driven Triggers
Each event fires a single time only if its precondition is met, ensuring surprises throughout your campaign.

Branching Storylines
Select choices in certain events to unlock follow-up scenarios that span multiple turns, deepening narrative impact.

Strategic Variety
From trade negotiations and public protests to diplomatic maneuvers and internal policy shifts, these events offer diverse tactical challenges.

Coming Soon:
We’re still refining the branching paths for Revolution and Trade events—expect richer interactions in future builds.

Dive into these new scenarios and discover how each decision shapes your nation’s fate!








[previewyoutube=yQUSsQpjunU;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Diplomacy & Alliances Go Live!
notes.content:
In this update we introduce our new Letter Diplomacy system:

Letter Funding: Send monetary support to rival parties through the in‑game correspondence UI.

Alliance Formation: Propose an alliance fee—if they accept, you gain their entire vote share for the next three turns.

Example: Your party sits at 40 % and you offer an alliance to Party B (10 %). Upon acceptance, your share jumps to 50 % while theirs drops to 0 % for three turns (subject to further in‑game actions).

Under‑Construction Features: The “Revolution” and “Trade” letter options are in place but not yet functional—stay tuned for full integration soon!

Watch the video above to see letter diplomacy and alliance mechanics in action, then dive in and reshape the political landscape of Statecraft!

[previewyoutube=KchK0u8pKNM;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.content:

🗃️ Almanac UI Added

👥 Demographic Breakdown
See total population counts by ideology, religion, and culture at a glance.

🤝 Party–Faction Dynamics

Dive into the data and sharpen your strategy with richer political intelligence!

notes.title: Intelligent AI Opponents Deployed!
notes.content:
In this update we’ve brought true competition to the table with our new AI system:

AI Decision Engine
Each turn, opponent AIs evaluate incoming events and pick options based on their own interests.

Tactical Manipulation Actions
When it suits them, AIs use Region Actions to sway local POP demographics or Selection Actions to tilt future event probabilities in their favor.

Self‑Serving Voting
Come election time, AI players reliably cast their ballots for their own party.

Revamped Election Screen
See at a glance which party took first place in each region (and with how many POPs), plus nationwide vote percentages for all parties.

Watch the video above to see your new, cunning rivals in action!

notes.title: End-Turn & Election Newspapers and Elections are Live!
notes.content:
With this update, Statecraft gets its very own in-game press:

🗳️ Presidential Elections
Once per cycle, cast your vote—either for yourself or another party—to choose the President for the next turn.

📊 Election Gazette
On the following turn, open the Election Newspaper to see each party’s vote share laid out in detail.

Every turn now comes with a wrap-up: learn which event option won, who backed it, and which actions were taken.

Stay on top of the political story as you write it—your strategy drives the headlines!

notes.title: UI & Fonts Overhauled!
notes.content:
In this patch we’ve tightened up the interface and laid the groundwork for full localization:

[previewyoutube=KKFE7S0_vjo;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Action Points & Region Manipulation Arrive!
notes.content:
In this update we’ve laid the groundwork for full-fledged actions—get ready to turn the tide of your nation with every decision:

[previewyoutube=duWJg5RL_3U;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

Action Points Added
A new resource, Action Points, now appears at the top-right of your screen (represented by pistol icons). Spend them to unlock powerful strategic moves each turn.

Event Probability Modifiers
Choose actions to increase or decrease the odds of specific event choices select in future turns—plan ahead and tilt fate in your favor.

Regional POP Manipulation
New actions let you directly influence a region’s population profiles—convert locals to your ideology or suppress opposing factions.

Under-the-Hood UI Placeholder
The action system is fully functional; for now you’ll see simple ID placeholders in the UI. Soon we’ll replace these with polished icons, tooltips, and animations.

Watch the video above to see these systems in action, then log in and start dictating history—Statecraft’s next evolution is here! Don’t forget to share your feedback and wishlist the game if you haven’t already.

notes.title: Events & Choices Now Live!

notes.title: Pop Features
notes.content:
As you saw in the trailer, we’ve introduced Pops—groups that each represent roughly 100,000 citizens—into Statecraft: Corrupted Democracy. Until now, Pops only carried a political affiliation. Today’s update adds two brand‑new attributes:

Culture ( Ulgan etc)

Religion ( Atheism etc)

Each Pop’s culture and religion will influence how they react to your policies, events, and diplomatic actions. In future patches, you’ll gain the tools to modify these variables—reshaping your nation’s identity from the ground up. Welcome to a more dynamic, belief‑driven world of politics: Statecraft has never felt so alive.

What’s Next?

New events tied to religious and cultural tensions

notes.title: Engine Change – Moving from Godot to Unity
notes.content:
Hello everyone, I'm EnginÇ., the game designer of Statecraft. Due to recent changes in our team, our game programmer and I have parted ways. As a result, I am now working on transitioning Statecraft to Unity, the game engine I am most familiar with.

Right now, I’m setting up basic UI elements, but since most assets are already prepared, I am aiming to release a minimal demo for the upcoming Steam Next Fest this summer.

notes.title: Spy Mechanic
notes.content:
We’ve introduced an exciting new Spy Mechanic to enhance your strategic options! Once you’ve completed the Diplomacy branch in the skill tree, you’ll gain access to powerful spy interactions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44900026/8d442404c50e808cb870f71a4426afe9f478cbe9.png[/img]

You can use spy actions via the Letter menu to monitor other players or political parties. By spying on your opponents, you can gain insight into their choices and even manipulate election outcomes. At the end of the turn, if you've spied on someone, you’ll see their selection and have the opportunity to change your choice or take additional actions with extra time.

But beware! If you don’t want others using spy actions against you, make sure to deploy a counter-spy. The counter-spy can mislead those who try to surveil you, sending them convincing yet false information, which will confuse their strategy and disrupt their plans.

Prepare to outmaneuver your opponents and take control of the political landscape with these new espionage tactics!

notes.title: Prologue Added to Urazya!
notes.content:
We’ve added a captivating prologue that sets the stage for your adventure in Urazya! This new feature explores the rich and tumultuous history of Urazya through three key chapters:

[h2]The Fall of the Empire[/h2]Discover the collapse of the grand Urazyan Empire.

[h2]The Rise of the Republic[/h2]Learn about the birth of the Republic and the challenges it faced during its formation.

[h2]The Age of Corruption[/h2]See how the struggle between East and West intensified, leading to an era of unprecedented corruption and turmoil.

Experience Urazya’s past through a newspaper at the game’s opening, giving you short insights into the world you are about to explore. This prologue enriches the narrative and provides crucial context for your journey. Enjoy the new lore.

notes.title: Skill Tree Added!
notes.content:
[h3]Types of skills:
[/h3]
[olist]
[*] Choice Skills: Many actions that you can use in main events such as parliamentary elections are unlocked with these skills. Manipulate the likelihood of each option being chosen. If you unlock them all the way, your spies will reveal most of your opponents' information to you.

[*]Regional Skills: Taking regional actions is crucial for strengthening the interest group that you endorse or weakening the interest groups you perceive as enemies. If you unlock them all the way, you will have 2 action points per turn instead of 1.

[*]Dangerous Lobby Relations: If you maintain good relations with an interest group, you can negotiate with their dangerous lobbies. Unlock this skill before making a deal, then ally with your opponents using lobbies.

[/olist]

notes.title: Extended Events
notes.content:
In normal events, even though events may branch out, they are resolved quickly within a short period, typically 3-7 turns.

In Extended Events, however, a response may trigger an event 10-20 turns later, and these events are major events. For example, The Great Migration or Nukelear Assault etc.

Note: For now, Extended Events simply consist of 2 events as a basic form of one cause, one effect, but we plan to create much more detailed Extended Events in the demo and subsequent periods.

notes.title: Beta Phase Incoming!
notes.content:
[h1]We’re excited to share that our game’s Alpha testing phase has concluded with flying colors!
[/h1]
 As we gear up for the Beta launch, you can look forward to an enriched gaming experience with the following already implemented mechanics and features:

[list]
[*] Dynamic main events that change each turn based on the country’s status.
[*] Two actionable options when clicking on cities.
[*] A working election mechanic that activates every six turns.
[*] Interest groups and a primitive rival AI in action.
[*] Three distinct game endings.
[*] An in-game newspaper feature.
[/list]

And that’s just the beginning! The Beta phase will introduce even more thrilling mechanics and features, including:

[list]
[*] The ability to send letters to sabotage other players and weave intrigue.
[*] Radical groups such as mafias, unions, and terrorists.
[*] A comprehensive skill tree.
[*] An increased number of main events.
[*] Additional game endings for more varied outcomes.
[*] Various government types and revolutions to navigate.
[*] A new menu, tutorial, and sounds to enhance your experience.
[*] Multiplayer and mod support to share the fun with friends and the community.
[/list]

Join us with Discord, in the Beta phase and be part of shaping the future of our game!
